space.name: Kitting Domain Layout 2
space.notes: Phase 4C B2 validation layout. Unlike layout0's symmetric design (transient centre crossing), this layout is built for SUSTAINED interference on the APPROACH leg: the robot's cheapest task and the human's first task target adjacent shelves reached by time-aligned approaches, so the two agents converge and then run near-parallel into the kitting table. Robot start is deliberately far from all shelves so the theta-crossing has room to land mid-approach, before pick_up, while abandoning the task is still cheap. No obstacles, no foreseeable tasks.

env_objects.notes: Shared delivery sink. Both agents' carry legs terminate here, so distance goes to zero for EVERY task pair — the discriminator between candidates is the approach leg and the early carry, not the minimum distance.
Robot's CHEAPEST task (approach 447 + carry 583 = 1033), so the greedy t=0 pick lands here by construction. 150 units from shelf_3 — this adjacency is what creates the sustained conflict.
Human's first target. Human approach is 449 against the robot's 447 — deliberately time-aligned so both agents arrive together rather than sequentially.

Robot's CLEAN ALTERNATIVE (total 1373). 340 steps dearer than item_4 — a real cost to switching, so B2 faces a genuine trade-off rather than a free escape. Its carry leg stays ~326 from the human's, roughly 2x clearer than item_4's.
Robot's third task (total 2029). Far enough east that it never competes — present to keep the pool at three, matching scenario_00.
Human's second target. At -36.9 deg from the human's start it is angularly far from shelf_3/4/6, so it does not muddy the early ambiguity.
Robot task 2 — the clean alternative B2 can escalate to.
